name: Payroll and Ghost-Employer Tax Fraud
description: Employers or labour providers underreport wages, create phantom workers, or operate short-lived 'ghost' companies that collect payroll funds and never remit social insurance or withholding tax. Common in labour-intensive sectors using subcontracting chains and agency labour.

sources.text: OECD, Shining Light on the Shadow Economy: Opportunities and Threats (2017)
FATF/OECD, Money Laundering Awareness Handbook for Tax Examiners and Tax Auditors (2012)
ILO and tax authority guidance on undeclared work and bogus self-employment
FATF and OECD, Money Laundering Awareness Handbook for Tax Examiners and Tax Auditors (2012)

exposure.rationale: Labour providers and ghost employers withdrawing cash payroll, paying workers via shared accounts, and bogus self-employment; employees are the payees.

indicators.name: Cash withdrawals match payroll amounts
indicators.desc: Large cash withdrawals shortly after receiving client funds, close to total weekly wages, with no matching payroll tax payments.
indicators.ctx: Large cash withdrawals shortly after receiving client funds, close to total weekly wages, with no matching payroll tax payments.
indicators.fp: Genuine cash-in-hand wages exist in some sectors.

indicators.name: Short-lived labour supplier with rotating entities
indicators.canon: Short-lived or rotating entities with common controllers
indicators.desc: Entities are repeatedly formed, abandoned or replaced by successors sharing directors, addresses or history of prior defaulted companies.
indicators.ctx: Company wound up or abandoned within one to two years, with successor firm at same address, same workers and clients.
indicators.fp: Contractors may restructure for commercial reasons.

indicators.name: Workers paid to multiple accounts or via third parties
indicators.canon: Workers paid to third-party or multiple accounts
indicators.desc: Wages are paid to accounts not held by the worker or split across several accounts.
indicators.ctx: Salaries are paid into accounts that control multiple 'employees' or into one account for numerous workers.
indicators.fp: Family or agency pooling can legitimately concentrate payments.

indicators.name: Payroll volume inconsistent with declared headcount
indicators.canon: Business revenue inconsistent with staffing or operating costs
indicators.desc: Reported revenue, payroll or resident staff do not match the typical costs and workforce of the stated business model.
indicators.ctx: Wages paid or invoiced greatly exceed declared staff and reported payroll tax. Labour provider shows no pension, insurance, equipment or accommodation costs.
indicators.fp: Seasonal hires may inflate volumes. New firms may have lean cost bases.

indicators.name: Sole-trader or bogus self-employment structure for large workforce
indicators.canon: Sole-trader or bogus self-employment structure for large workforce
indicators.desc: Many workers treated as independent contractors despite working under direction for one client.
indicators.ctx: Many workers treated as independent contractors despite working under direction for one client.
indicators.fp: Contracting is lawful where genuinely independent.

indicators.name: Payments to workers just under tax or reporting thresholds
indicators.canon: Payments to workers just under tax or reporting thresholds
indicators.desc: Pay split into amounts staying below withholding or reporting thresholds.
indicators.ctx: Pay split into amounts staying below withholding or reporting thresholds.
indicators.fp: Part-time work may legitimately fall below thresholds.

indicators.name: Multiple businesses sharing addresses, phones and bank signatories
indicators.desc: Several apparently separate businesses or sub-accounts share owners, signatories, addresses, devices or bank accounts.
indicators.ctx: A group of firms pooling workers share control and registered details with no group disclosed.
indicators.fp: Business parks and accountants' addresses are shared.
